title: Stability, Budget Triangle, and Rollout Timeline Sync

SE to validate ded- pool latency under burst; CSM to coordinate pilot dates and internal stakeholders. Agreement to run a 24h burn and share results by next Wednesday; follow-up exec sync planned.

Rollout timeline for model v2.0 (canary plan)

Who owns on-call for inference in NovusCart's infra?
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for making time. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Aisha: Hi, Aisha Thompson here, Head of MLOps at NovusCart.
[00:09] Diego: Diego Ramirez, Platform. Morning.
[00:11] Claire: Claire Wu, VP Product.
[00:14] Jordan (SE): Jordan Park from Redwood, SE.
[00:16] Samir (CSM): Samir Patel, CSM.
[00:18] Maya: Awesome. Agenda — quick status on the usage ramp you saw last week, cost impact, dedicated vs host decision, and rollout timeline for v2.0. Cool?
[00:28] Aisha: Yep that's right, we saw like a 2.7x uplift in token throughput Friday through Sunday. It spiked on the recommendation path.
[00:35] Diego: It's the recommendation path plus a batch job that went rogue, but that's partly on us. The important bit is p99 latency jumped from ~420ms to 1.3s for a window.
[00:44] Jordan: Got it. Do you have the trace ids or sample requests? Even a small set helps us repro on our side.
[00:49] Aisha: Sent a bucket of traces to the shared sheet — there's a .csv. Some of the tokens are long — like 2k sequences — and we suspect KV cache invalidation churn.
[00:59] Jordan: Long sequences definitely change kernel selection; if the runtime keeps switching execution paths during the burst that can spike p99. Could be batching thresholds too.
[01:07] Claire: This is why product is worried — checkout latency is consumer-facing. We have a target of p99 < 500ms end-to-end.
[01:14] Maya: Good — now the budget triangle: latency, cost, reliability. We want to map levers. Jordan, could you walk through what we can do on the runtime side?
[01:22] Jordan: Sure. Short list: 1) Dedicated pools with pinned capacity reduce noisy neighbor effects — predictable tail. 2) Autoscale policies with burst capacity — cheaper but can still have warmup penalty. 3) Configuring prefix/KV cache retention and hot-shard placement reduces recompute. 4) Quantize model to int8 for less GPU memory — may impact quality slightly. Also runtime continuous-batching knobs: smaller max batch size lowers queuing latency but increases per-token cost.
[01:45] Diego: How big is the quality hit on int8 quant? For our recommendation models we need top-N fidelity preserved.
[01:51] Jordan: For most decoder-only models, int8 gives a very small drop on ranking, like 0.5–1.5% on internal benchmarks, but it really depends on the model and metric. We can run a two-day eval with your eval set.
[02:02] Samir: Also, we can suggest a hybrid: keep critical checkout route on higher precision/dedicated, run background ranking on quantized. That splits cost.
[02:10] Aisha: That sounds promising. What about caching? You mentioned prefix cache churn — we saw a lot of cache misses during the spike.
[02:16] Jordan: Right — if the workload has many long tails, the cache eviction policy might be thrashing. We can tune TTLs and hot-key pinning. Also checkpointing of the KV cache across workers helps with cold-starts for canaries.
[02:27] Claire: Timeline for v2.0 rollout — product wants a staged canary starting in two weeks and full roll in six weeks. Is that feasible?
[02:35] Maya: Two weeks is tight but possible if we scope the canary to 5% traffic and you give us the target payloads. We need to validate latency under that traffic first.
[02:43] Diego: Another question — if we move checkout to Redwood Dedicated, what's the lead time to reserve capacity and what happens to bursts?
[02:50] Maya: Reserved pools can be provisioned in 3–5 business days for standard configurations, faster for preferred zones. For bursts, we offer two options: auto-burst into shared capacity (with doced fallbacks) or pre-configured burst instances that warm faster. Each has cost tradeoffs.
[03:06] Aisha: Cost-wise we are tight this quarter. We need clear scenarios showing incremental cost vs expected p99 reduction.
[03:12] Maya: Understood. I'll send three pricing scenarios: 1) fully hosted with autoscale, 2) reserved-dedicated for checkout + hosted for non-critical, 3) reserved + pre-warmed burst.
[03:22] Jordan: For the 24-hour burn test, we can replay your production traces against a replica of your checkout route in a dedicated pool. That'll give p50/p95/p99 distribution and memory/throughput stats.
[03:31] Diego: Will that interfere with our current traffic? We prefer a shadow test.
[03:34] Jordan: We'll run it isolated against a provisioned pool; no impact on production. We just need the trace files and a list of headers.
[03:41] Claire: Security quick check — we need to keep embeddings retention for product search to 30 days and ensure KMS is customer-managed.
[03:47] Samir: We support customer KMS and you can set retention policies per-route. I will post the SOC2 / retention whitepaper after the call.
[03:54] Aisha: Also SSO — we use Okta and want RBAC aligned to our groups.
[03:58] Maya: We do SAML/Okta SSO and map roles to RBAC. Samir will include the exact claim mappings.
[04:05] Diego: One more infra detail — during the spike we saw GPU memory fragmentation across pods. Any mitigation?
[04:12] Jordan: Fragmentation can be improved by packing with model quantization and by tuning pooling size. Also consider using fewer larger workers rather than many small ones to reduce cross-pod memory churn. There's a tradeoff with tail latency though.
[04:24] Claire: Okay, can we recap deliverables?
[04:27] Maya: Sure. Jordan runs the 24h burn and uploads logs. Samir sends security + SSO docs. Maya sends pricing scenarios. NovusCart confirms pilot windows. We also agreed to an exec-level 30-minute sync after results.
[04:40] Aisha: We want the results before our next platform review on the 21st.
[04:43] Samir: We'll aim to have the initial report by the 20th so you have one day to review.
[04:48] Diego: Quick nit — in the traces you'll see some request ids with truncated prompts, transcription of the file names might be off, sorry if that causes confusion.
[04:55] Jordan: No worries, we'll correlate with timestamps. If something doesn't match we'll ping you.
[04:59] Maya: Anything else?
[05:02] Claire: Curious — did you see any mention of Vertex or Anthropic in the internal evals? We're evaluating alternatives.
[05:07] Maya: Common question — some teams run hybrid: fast paths on hosted and experimental on hosted alternatives. But pay attention to integration complexity and observability gaps.
[05:16] Aisha: Ok that's great, thanks everyone. We'll get the pilot windows over today.
[05:20] Maya: Thanks all. We'll follow up with the docs and schedule for the burn.
[05:24] Samir: Thanks, bye.
[05:26] (call ends)
file_notes: Transcript contains minor transcription artifacts (e.g., 'K V cache' for KV cache, 'ded pool' shorthand). References to shared sheet and traces are links noted in the CRM record.
